sentence: This project studies how metals in the environment early in life affect lung growth, using metals measured in deciduous teeth.
This project builds expertise in research ethics, which protects ordinary people from exploitation.
This project studies how interleukin 33 is regulated in epithelial cells and looks for inhibitors of it.
This project studies how HIV co-infections and other conditions change the circadian rhythm of liver cells, using cell culture models and humanized mice.
This project studies how the protein ninjurin1, which ruptures the plasma membrane during programmed cell death, is regulated.
This project studies rare genetic variants and clinical data in children with structural epilepsies and brain tumors to follow how their disease develops.
This project uses mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance and cryo-electron microscopy to study protein structures in the viral replication cycle.
This project uses existing data to study how extreme heat affects health and builds early warnings of dangerous heat periods.
This project studies whether hair cells in the vestibular organs of mice and humans can regenerate, and how that affects their function.
This project uses data from many sudden cardiac arrest cases to find mitochondrial genetic variants linked to arrest risk and resuscitation outcomes.
This project studies how genes are regulated during mammalian digit tip regeneration, to understand limits on regeneration of human limbs.
This project builds imaging tools that separate cellular and macromolecular development across the brain, to understand brain maturation.
This project tests a pressure-sensitive bioadhesive tape that sticks to wet tissue and can be removed, for use in minimally invasive surgeries.
This project builds explainable machine learning tools that show how targeted stimulation changes connectivity across brain areas.
This project studies how mu opioid receptors and enkephalin influence the maturation of respiratory neurons and breathing development.
This project builds computational and deep learning methods that improve how images from label-free optical microscopy are formed and analyzed.
This project uses a technology to disturb noncoding genetic elements in vivo to find out what they do in development and behavior.
This project studies how a photoreceptor-specific transcriptional cofactor controls gene expression in rod and cone cells.
This project studies how signaling molecules cause loss of the tight junction protein claudin-5 in blood-brain barrier cells during neuroinflammation.
This project builds machine learning methods to improve the accuracy of amide proton transfer imaging, using partially synthetic data.
